bullets.title: Global chip selloff deepens on AI spending concerns, KOSPI crash
bullets.body: Semiconductor stocks extended losses in premarket trading, with the sector down 3%+ while broader market trades flat to higher. South Korea's KOSPI halted after crashing 10.8%—its 2nd-biggest single-day drop on record—driven by margin calls on leveraged ETF products and concerns about China's advancing chipmaking capabilities. Korea's AI bubble unwind is being called a 'canary' for broader AI sentiment.

bullets.title: Morgan Stanley stays bullish on AI supply chain despite pullback
bullets.body: Morgan Stanley maintains a bullish stance on the AI supply chain, calling the recent selloff driven by profit-taking and technical factors rather than fundamental deterioration. The firm expects AI compute demand to outpace supply for years, framing the pullback as an attractive risk/reward entry.

bullets.title: META and BlackRock announce $14B Texas data center joint venture
bullets.body: Meta and BlackRock are establishing a joint venture to develop a 1-gigawatt data center campus in El Paso, Texas at an estimated $14B total cost (buildings, power, cooling, connectivity), expected to come online by 2028. Separately, Meta priced a $12.5B debt offering for data center projects Monday at higher rates than a comparable deal last year, as hyperscaler CDS spreads blow out to new record wides.

bullets.title: Nvidia backing AI financing boom; in talks to guarantee OpenAI deal
bullets.body: Nvidia is reportedly in talks to guarantee financing for OpenAI, deploying its balance sheet to support the broader AI investment cycle. Apple has also reclaimed the title of world's most valuable company from Nvidia after 10 months.

bullets.title: Amazon overhauling AI strategy, winding down most flagship models
bullets.body: Amazon is discontinuing the majority of its flagship AI models in a major strategic overhaul, signaling struggles in the competitive AI race. Separately, satellite images reportedly show Amazon data center facilities in Iran were damaged in strikes, with unclear operational impact on AWS.

bullets.title: TSLA bear thesis: 175x FY'26 P/E seen as excessive as AI multiples unwind
bullets.body: One fintwit analyst expects TSLA to fall below $300/share, citing a FY'26 P/E in excess of 175x as AI-related valuations unwind broadly. The call circulated multiple times with consistent framing around excessive valuation relative to fundamentals.

bullets.title: Grok called MU a 'strong buy' two days after its all-time high
bullets.body: Grok recommended Micron as a strong buy on June 27, two days after it had closed at an all-time high, citing explosive AI demand. A competing AI advisor (Frank) had recommended staying on the sidelines—underscoring divergent AI-generated investment signals in the semiconductor space.

bullets.title: Tech sector correction context: current -12% drawdown shallow by history
bullets.body: The technology sector is down 12% from its peak after 56 days—described as 'one of the shallowest corrections on record.' The median historical tech selloff drops 25.7% and takes 73 days to bottom; all prior drawdowns have ultimately recovered to new all-time highs.

bullets.title: Fintwit bag-holding warning on GOOGL, AMZN as signals shift
bullets.body: One analyst flagged a risk of 'bag-holding' in prolonged profitable tech positions like Google and Amazon, noting that while narratives haven't changed, underlying signals have. The longer a position stays profitable, the more susceptible the holder becomes to rationalizing the narrative.

bullets.title: AI automation cutting thousands of customer service jobs at MSFT, UBER
bullets.body: Microsoft (which cut 10,000 service-division headcount in recent years) and Uber are among companies deploying AI-powered systems to automate customer service chat and call centers. The structural workforce impact is described as already underway across multiple industries.

bullets.title: Fed dynamics shifting: Citadel expects hike; market pricing 35-40% probability
bullets.body: Citadel Securities expects the Fed to raise interest rates this week. A fintwit macro commentator argues traditional Fed frameworks no longer apply, citing a 'family fight' at the Fed with Waller publicly challenging Warsh, and 3-6 likely dissenters on the next decision. Market pricing implies 35-40% probability of a hike; oil is also 10% higher than at the last FOMC meeting.

bullets.title: JPMorgan turns bullish on stocks broadly
bullets.body: JPMorgan has shifted to a bullish stance on equities, per breaking newswire. No specific sector or ticker guidance was provided in the announcement.

bullets.title: BCA equity risk indicator at +1 SD above mean—historically a pullback signal
bullets.body: BCA's US Equity Risk Indicator is one standard deviation above its historical mean, a level that has historically preceded major S&P 500 pullbacks according to the model's track record.

bullets.title: China immersion DUV progress 'overblown' per fintwit analyst
bullets.body: One tech analyst argues China's immersion DUV chipmaking advance is overstated: ASML developed this technology in 2008, and while it achieves 28nm nodes in a single shot, reaching 7nm requires multi-patterning—a meaningful practical barrier. The analyst concedes China's progress is still material despite the hype.

bullets.title: Investor patience on AI/tech capex cycle visibly eroding
bullets.body: John Authers' daily note flagged that 'investors are growing less patient about funding the investment cycle with uncertain payoff,' and fintwit commentary echoes the view that 'circular financing is bad' sentiment is cycling back. Hyperscaler CDS spreads hitting record wides amplifies the credit stress signal.

bullets.title: Semis diverging sharply from rest of market; software trades opposite AI stocks
bullets.body: Semiconductors are down 3%+ on the session while the broader market trades flat to higher—a notable divergence. One trader also noted that pure tech ETFs (MU, INTC) are trading in the opposite direction from high-flying AI software names, suggesting rotation dynamics within the tech complex.

bullets.title: BofA: lower-income spending now outpacing higher-income, K-shape trend ends
bullets.body: Bank of America card data shows lower-income households now posting stronger spending growth than higher-income, reversing the K-shaped trend. BofA attributes the shift to stronger labor income and lower fuel costs—a positive signal for consumer-facing sectors.

bullets.title: US-Iran pause drives oil down 3.5% to ~$85/bbl (Brent)
bullets.body: Brent crude fell 3.5% to approximately $85 on hopes of a Hormuz Strait reopening amid a U.S.-Iran pause, contributing to lower Treasury yields. OPEC+ separately expects to hold 2026 output steady after September.
